newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish MP testifies on security scandal.
newsitem.headline: Turkish MP testifies on security scandal.

text.p: A Turkish MP at the centre of a security scandal linking the state with underworld gangs gave evidence before a parliamentary commission investigating the charges on Tuesday.
The scandal erupted last November after the deputy, Sedat Bucak, was injured in a car crash in which a top policeman and a wanted gangster both died.
"We asked all necessary questions and he (Bucak) answered all of them," the commission chief Mehmet Elkatmis told reporters after the meeting, which was closed to the media.

Parliamentary sources close to the commission told Reuters that Bucak had described events leading to the unlikely combination of passengers being in the same car along with seven pistols and two silencers.
"The guns weren't mine. Catli apparently put them there," Bucak said, referring to Abdullah Catli, the convicted heroin smuggler and alleged mafia boss who died in the crash.

A series of media reports following the crash have linked senior officials to far-right gangsters alleged to have carried out political killings and dirty work for the state in its fight against far-left groups and Kurdish rebels.

Bucak and former interior minister Mehmet Agar, who resigned after the crash, face possible criminal charges over the scandal if their parliament immunities are lifted as a result of the investigation.

Bucak is an MP for the True Path Party (DYP) and the head of a large anti-rebel Kurdish militia sponsored by the state in southeastern Turkey. He is being investigated on charges of concealing the wanted Catli.
Agar is being investigated on a charge of signing a false police document for Catli.
Justice Minister Sevket Kazan said last week his ministry would approve any prosecutor's request to lift the MPs' immunity.
